clue.text: Obscure diarist

explanation.surface: A little-known keeper of a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: An insignificant person is a nobody, and Grossmith's comic Diary of a Nobody is written by one.

clue.text: Lotuses provided for what may be noble sum

indicators.note: what the letters may be once rearranged, so the words noble sum are a scrambled form

explanation.surface: Lotus flowers offered in exchange for a grand payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs backwards in spirit: the answer, rearranged, may be 'noble sum', and those letters reshuffled give the plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of the sacred lotus, so its plural names lotus plants.

clue.text: Large sort of legs for flying ace

indicators.note: a sort of legs is a rearranged version of the word legs

explanation.surface: A pilot with outsize, oddly shaped legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges LEGS into GLES. Biggles is the fictional fighter pilot of W.E. Johns's boys' adventure books.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain W.E. Johns's hero is a celebrated fictional airman of the First World War.

clue.text: Your old place in terribly dim bar suggests rapturous poem

indicators.note: an instruction to put one piece inside another
terribly signals the letters of dim bar are jumbled

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Seeing an archaic phrase in a seedy dim bar hints at an ecstatic ode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns DIM BAR into DIRAMB, and 'place in' puts THY inside it after DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb was a wild choral hymn to Dionysus, so the word now means any frenzied, ecstatic verse.

clue.text: Folk like Leibniz and Pangloss?

parts.note: Leibniz held this is the best of all possible worlds, and Voltaire's Pangloss parrots him: believers in an ideal state of things

explanation.surface: A question about a philosopher and his satirical copy in Candide.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealists who imagine a perfect world are dreamers of that kind, as Pangloss's 'best of all possible worlds' is.

clue.text: 9's ragamuffin

explanation.surface: A shabby urchin belonging to another clue's author.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is John Galsworthy, who published a story collection under this title in 1920.
explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy's 1920 book of stories bears the title, and the word itself means a person in ragged clothes.

clue.text: Outstanding, like Fred Urquhart's captive lady

explanation.surface: Something prominent, compared with a caged heroine of Scottish fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Urquhart, a Scottish novelist, wrote Proud Lady in a Cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing out from a surface is the sense of this adjective, and Urquhart's caged lady is described by it in his title.

clue.text: Symphonic poet with Bohemian lifestyle

parts.note: a composer of symphonic poems who lived as a Bohemian, that is a Czech, not an unconventional artist

explanation.surface: A free-living artist who writes symphonic verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bohemian lifestyle' suggests an unconventional artist, but here it means life in Bohemia: the Czech composer of the cycle Ma vlast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech composer wrote the symphonic poems of Ma vlast and was born in Bohemia.

clue.text: French painter portrays young relative with ancient line

parts.note: sis is a familiar word for a younger sister
a ley is a supposed ancient line linking prehistoric sites

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a youngster with an old family line.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Sisley was an Impressionist landscape artist working in France.

clue.text: Nobel Prizewinner said to have shown foresight

explanation.surface: A laureate reputed to have been far-sighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foresight' sounds like Forsyte: he showed the Forsytes in The Forsyte Saga, and won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1932.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist won the 1932 Nobel Prize for Literature and wrote the saga of the Forsyte family.

clue.text: Nance, Patrick White's golden-hearted girl, inverts stage illumination

indicators.note: inverts swaps the two halves of the word over, so the end comes to the front

parts.note: a footlight is one of the lamps along the front of a stage

explanation.surface: An Australian novelist's kindly heroine turns the stage lights upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverts' moves the front half of FOOTLIGHT to the end. Nance is a character in Patrick White's The Tree of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to Nance, the warm-hearted girl in Patrick White's novel.

clue.text: Playwright's name recalled during wasted opening night .

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards
during says the letters lie inside the words wasted opening

explanation.surface: A dramatist's name is remembered through a disastrous premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' points inside 'waSTED Opening', and 'recalled' turns STEDO round. Clifford Odets was an American dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Clifford Odets was the American dramatist of Waiting for Lefty and Golden Boy.

clue.text: Burgess trilogy from Curious Animal, a Yankee and Other Stories

annotationWithheld.why: Burgess trilogy from Curious Animal, a Yankee and Other Stories (7): ANIMAL + A + Y gives eight letters with an I too many, and no clue word removes it
annotationWithheld.clue: Burgess trilogy from Curious Animal, a Yankee and Other Stories

clue.text: Beckett work possibly leading to a mate

explanation.surface: A play by Beckett that might end in checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's one-act play has the chess term as its title, the final phase of play when checkmate comes.

clue.text: Nameless bard, or Italian

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Ossian is the legendary Gaelic bard of Macpherson's poems

explanation.surface: An anonymous poet, or perhaps one from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name. Ossia is a musical term for an alternative passage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italian the word means 'or else', used in scores to mark an alternative reading.

clue.text: Successful college boat described by Robert Hillyer?

explanation.surface: A winning college crew written about by an American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The college crew that finishes first in bumps races is 'Head of the River'; Robert Hillyer wrote a novel called Riverhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading boat in college rowing is head of the river, and the American poet Hillyer wrote a novel of that title.

clue.text: Successful takeover bidders, like Antonio of Milan, and Duke Frederick

definitions.text: like Antonio of Milan, and Duke Frederick

explanation.surface: Corporate raiders compared with two Shakespeare villains.
explanation.walkthrough: Antonio seizes his brother Prospero's dukedom of Milan in The Tempest; Duke Frederick takes his brother's dukedom in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who seize a throne by force resemble Antonio and Frederick, who each displaced a ducal brother.

clue.text: "Home went Violante and ed all " (Browning)

parts.note: a line from The Ring and the Book with the verb missing: Violante went home and revealed all her secrets

explanation.surface: A quotation from Browning with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in the line from Browning's The Ring and the Book; the missing verb means confided her secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: To unburden one's breast is to confess everything, which Violante does in Browning's poem.

clue.text: Sort of research carried out by Jules Verne?

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of investigation a French novelist made.
explanation.walkthrough: Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea explores the ocean deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough study is described by this phrase, and Verne's undersea voyages went literally deep down.

clue.text: A man writing a panegyric may keep them out of sight, suggested Samuel Johnson

definitions.text: A man writing a panegyric may keep them out of sight, suggested Samuel Johnson

parts.words: A man writing a panegyric may keep them out of sight, suggested Samuel Johnson
parts.note: Johnson said that a eulogist is not on oath and may leave out the subject's faults and moral failings

explanation.surface: Johnson's view that a writer of praise can hide unflattering things.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy passes over its subject's moral failings, the bad habits Johnson said the writer may conceal.

clue.text: Star port of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: A celebrated harbour of the pharaohs.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright star in Carina shares its name with a coastal town of Egypt near Alexandria in ancient times.

clue.text: "I should ("be proud to have my memory anna Akhmatova", Epilogue)

definitions.text: "I should ("be proud to have my memory anna Akhmatova", Epilogue)

parts.words: "I should ("be proud to have my memory anna Akhmatova", Epilogue)
parts.note: a line from the Epilogue of Akhmatova's Requiem with its last word missing: the poet would be honoured to have her memory adorned

explanation.surface: A quotation from Anna Akhmatova with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in the Epilogue of Akhmatova's Requiem; the missing verb means honoured or adorned.
explanation.definitionFit: To have one's memory honoured is to have it adorned, the sense the missing participle carries.

clue.text: Random father

parts.note: Random is Smollett's hero Roderick Random, whose lost father reappears in South America under a Spanish name

explanation.surface: Any old dad picked at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Random' looks like an adjective, but it is Roderick Random, hero of Smollett's novel; his father turns up as Don Rodrigo.
explanation.definitionFit: In Smollett's novel the hero's long-lost father is the rich Don Rodrigo.

clue.text: Passage from it inconclusive for Mrs Moore

definitions.text: Passage from it inconclusive for Mrs Moore

parts.words: Passage from it inconclusive for Mrs Moore
parts.note: Mrs Moore in Forster's A Passage to ... travels there, but her journey out of it ends without arrival, as she dies at sea

explanation.surface: An extract that leaves a character's story unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: In Forster's A Passage to India, Mrs Moore sails home but dies at sea, so her passage from the country is never completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Forster's novel takes Mrs Moore to the subcontinent, and her voyage back from it never ends.

clue.text: Give short-story writer a ring. If you can remember his name

definitions.text: Give short-story writer a ring. If you can remember his name

parts.words: Give short-story writer a ring. If you can remember his name
parts.note: the American short-story writer's first name was Ring, so giving him a ring supplies his forename

explanation.surface: Phone the author, if his name comes back to you.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring Lardner was an American short-story writer and sports journalist; 'a ring' is his forename, not a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring Lardner wrote American short stories such as Haircut.

clue.text: Unconscious follow-up to trophy for heart doctor

indicators.note: follow-up to places the second piece straight after the first

parts.note: a cup is a sporting trophy
the id is Freud's name for the unconscious part of the mind

explanation.surface: A cardiologist sees what follows winning a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart doctor' is no cardiologist: the god of love mends or wounds hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love deals in matters of the heart, a playful sense of physician.

clue.text: A couple of Milne's works

explanation.surface: Two books by the author of Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.walkthrough: A.A. Milne wrote a 1931 novel with this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of persons make a couple, and Milne's novel of a married pair has that title.

clue.text: No Haydn I played recalled Hungarian pianist

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: A pianist remembered for not performing Haydn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges NO HAYDN I. Erno Dohnanyi was a Hungarian pianist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erno Dohnanyi was a Hungarian concert pianist, composer and conductor.
